column1: # English words of the catalog (job 470, languages.ts). Format: word<TAB>category[<TAB>concept[<TAB>forms]].
# word: what the English catalog offers, lowercase, as an English list writes it (apples, milk).
# category: one of dictionary.tsv's 17 seed keys; categories and stores are the same in every language.
# concept: the dictionary.tsv term the word is (milk -> milch). The word then takes the concept's
#   category and canonical key, so Milch and milk are one item for the duplicate hint, the
#   household's corrections and the store memory. Empty: the word is a concept of its own
#   (a classifier_terms row with lang en). A word that is a German term too names it as concept.
# forms: other spellings, comma-separated: misspellings, irregular plurals, US/UK spellings that
#   are no word of their own, and the plural of a singular word (avocado: avocados). The generator
#   adds the singular of a plural word itself (languages.ts, englishInflections); a listed form
# A US/UK pair that both sides write (eggplant, aubergine) is two words on one concept.
# Placement follows dictionary.tsv's header (spreads pantry, plant milks chilled, baby care drugstore,
# pet food household). The classifier reads every language's forms, so an English name sorts the
# same for every member of a household; the app offers the words of its language.
# From synonyms.tsv's English section (job 51), the words Siri hears most
